lines.text: Mayon rumbles, and the alert goes up.
lines.screen: Night sky; the cone of Mayon draws in with a thin ash plume and a glowing summit. On “alert” a badge “ALERT LEVEL 3” flashes, with the chip “January 6, 2026 · PHIVOLCS raises Mayon to Alert Level 3” (source: Interaksyon/Philstar, Jan 6, 2026).

lines.text: A family in the six-kilometer danger zone must leave.
lines.screen: The 6-km Permanent Danger Zone ring draws around the base. A house inside it; a mother, Lolo with a cane and a schoolgirl with a backpack step out and start walking. Label “preemptive evacuation”.

lines.text: Which shelter has room? Can Lolo get in? How far is it?
lines.screen: Three tags pop in, one per question: “Which shelter has room?” · “Can Lolo get in?” (wheelchair-ramp icon) · “How far is it?” (clock).

lines.text: And if it is a classroom, whose class stops?
lines.screen: A fourth tag in gold: “Whose class stops?” A classroom (board and desks) appears; on “stops” a red stamp “CLASS SUSPENDED” lands on the board.

lines.text: Our shelter model answers all of it.
lines.screen: The LIGTA-S badge appears; on “all” the four tags turn gold with check marks. Under the badge: “where to go · is there room · can they get in · how long · which classrooms”.

lines.text: Zoom out.
lines.screen: The family scene shrinks away. Albay card: 18 cities and municipalities · 720 barangays · 1,374,768 residents (PSA 2020 census); a field of 720 dots, one per barangay.

lines.text: In January, four schools became shelters, and thousands of learners were affected.
lines.screen: Four school icons turn into evacuation centers. Counters: “3,424 learners affected” and “608 learners displaced from the danger zone”; “some schools shifted to modular or blended learning” (Philippine Daily Inquirer, 2026).

lines.text: In May, Camalig classrooms were sheltering families.
lines.screen: 34 classroom tiles fill one by one: “34 classrooms in three Camalig schools · 488 families, about 1,315 people” (Daily Tribune, May 4, 2026); chip “ashfall reached up to 132 schools” (Philippine Star, May 6, 2026).

lines.text: The law says classrooms should come last.
lines.screen: Card “RA 10821 (2016): schools only when no other suitable space exists”; a three-step ladder: non-school space → school gym or open space → classrooms (last resort, at most 15 days unless the LGU documents the need); chip “RA 12076 (2024): a Ligtas Pinoy Center in every city and municipality”.

lines.text: SDGs 4, 11, and 13 ask for safe schools and safer towns.
lines.screen: Three goal chips: SDG 4.a safe learning environments · SDG 11.5 fewer people affected by disasters · SDG 13.1 resilience to climate hazards.

lines.text: Yet no tool told a town how many classrooms it truly needs.
lines.screen: A row of classrooms with question marks; the notation “classrooms needed = ?” in gold.

lines.text: Now, the evacuation.
lines.screen: The synthetic test network E1 draws in: summit, ring road, five towns, six barangay clusters, shelters. Label “TEST NETWORK E1 · synthetic volcano, not Albay data”.

lines.text: On our test network, three barangays must leave.
lines.screen: O1, O2 and O3 inside the 6-km zone pulse red. Card “Alert Level 3 · 1,560 evacuees · 342 vulnerable”.

lines.text: Send everyone to the nearest shelter, and nearly three hundred find it full.
lines.screen: Dots stream from each barangay to its nearest shelter site; the northeast and east sites overflow and flash FULL; counter “298 arrive at full shelters”.

lines.text: A plan that counts only minutes fills the nearest classrooms.
lines.screen: “Time-only plan”: classroom grids of the three schools (20, 30 and 14 rooms) fill in red: 40 classrooms closed · 1,702 learners displaced · mean trip 29.48 min.

lines.text: If a lahar takes the bridges, four hundred fifty are cut off.
lines.screen: Alert Level 4 with lahar: channels A and B flow down the south flank; the seven bridges A1–A4 and B1–B3 get a red X; the southern pocket (O3, O4 and one school, SCH1) is shaded: “450 residents cannot be sheltered”.

lines.text: Room, time, and school all pull against each other.
lines.screen: Three chips ROOM · TIME · SCHOOL appear on a triangle, joined by straining lines.

lines.text: So, where does MCS come in?
lines.screen: Faint math symbols drift behind. On “MCS” the gold letters M, C, S drop in one by one, then unfold into Mathematical · Computational · Sciences. The stakes bar reaches its top rung, “MCS”.

lines.text: Mathematics turns open data on roads and shelters into a graph.
lines.screen: The title shrinks into an MCS badge and a chain appears across the top: Open data → Graph → Algorithm → Numbers → Optimisation → Proof (“Open data” and “Graph” light up). Panel MATHEMATICS: G = (N, E) with travel time τ_e and capacity u_e; σ = (active hazard zones, closed bridges); D_a, V_a. The test network builds road by road.

lines.text: At Sphere's three and a half square meters, a classroom holds eighteen.
lines.screen: c_s = ⌊A_s / 3.5 m²⌋; q = ⌊(7 m × 9 m) / 3.5 m²⌋ = 18; a 7 × 9 m classroom fills with 18 figures; three shelter tiers: tier 0 non-school space, tier 1 school open space, tier 2 classrooms; K_s = ⌈y_s / 18⌉.

lines.text: Computing places everyone with one minimum-cost flow, in whole numbers.
lines.screen: “Algorithm” lights. Panel COMPUTING: Algorithm 1 steps highlight in turn; cost(a, s, ι) = T_σ(a, s) + M_O·1[ι = 1] + M_Y·1[ι = 2]; x ∈ ℤ≥0 (“no evacuee is split between shelters”). On the test network the Alert Level 3 plan streams along the roads.

lines.text: A copy of the roads per minute gives the exact clearance time.
lines.screen: “Numbers” lights. A small time-expanded network (one layer per minute); T*_σ = min{T ≥ 0 : F_σ(T) = D′}; bisection probes 8, 16, 32, 64, then 31, 47, 55, 51, 53, 52; the arrival curve F(T) climbs to 1,560 at T* = 53 min, with the lower bound 34 min dashed (test network).

lines.text: Optimisation follows the law: vulnerable first, then everyone, classrooms last.
lines.screen: “Optimisation” lights. Panel OPTIMISATION: max F_V ≻ max F ≻ min Y ≻ min O ≻ min Θ, each level glowing on its word; M_O = D·T_max + 1, M_Y = D·(M_O + T_max) + 1.

lines.text: On the test network: fourteen classrooms closed, not forty, for under two minutes more travel.
lines.screen: Classroom grids drop from 40 red rooms to 14; bars: time-only 40 rooms · 1,702 learners · 29.48 min against school-preserving 14 rooms · 532 learners · 31.18 min (+1.70 min).

lines.text: When a lahar cuts off a pocket, a greedy rule picks the next Ligtas Pinoy Center.
lines.screen: Both lahar channels close their bridges; the southern pocket shades. f(S) = Φ_θ(E ∪ S) − Φ_θ(E) is monotone submodular, so f(S_g) ≥ (1 − 1/e) f(S*) ≈ 0.632 f(S*). A gold star lands on the south town: “400 of the 450 sheltered”; second site, northeast town: “persons in classrooms 920 → 570”; “greedy = exhaustive best for k = 1 to 3” (test network).

lines.text: Ten results, proven, then verified.
lines.screen: “Proof” lights. Ten tiles, Propositions 1 to 10, get a proof mark ∎ on “proven” and a check on “verified”, with the checks: 300/300 plans · 150/150 bound · 660/660 · 79/79 · 0 of 4,796 · greedy worst 0.890. Footer: “Each proven on paper, then checked against independent code on synthetic instances · no field data”.

lines.text: LIGTA-S cannot build a single new shelter.
lines.screen: Conclusion. A boom just before the line clears the screen to a plain background. The line appears large, with “single new shelter” in gold. The large text is its subtitle.

lines.text: But once towns list their shelters, it shows each family where to go, and keeps more classrooms open.
lines.screen: Appears under it in two rows, with “where to go” and “more classrooms open” in gold. Both lines then fade out.

lines.text: The nearest shelter is not always the right one.
lines.screen: [pause] The screen is empty for a moment. Then the line appears, with the LIGTA-S badge and the paper title below.

lines.text: The right plan keeps families safe and schools open.
lines.screen: Lands in large gold type with a final hit; “safe” and “open” are underlined. Hold silence.
